Yes, in one respect: I changed the test file, and that is the only thing beyond implementing the specified behavior.

I added an autouse fixture to `tests/test_game.py` that patches `normalize_word`, `is_valid_word`, `get_random_word` and `score_guess` with stand-ins. Without it the tests would fail, because those modules are still `NotImplementedError` stubs. I also added one test, `test_invalid_and_game_over`, and extended the test imports to include `Feedback`. The assignment allows test edits for cross-module dependencies.

The consequence is that the passing tests show `Game`'s state logic works. They don't show it works with the real dictionary or scorer. The stand-in `is_valid_word` only checks that a word is five letters and alphabetic, so "WRONG" passes validation in the tests. The real dictionary might reject it, and then `test_game_over_after_six_attempts` would fail. That's a risk once the real modules are merged.

I did not special-case any test inputs in `wordle/game.py`. I did not touch config files or any file outside my allowed list. Nothing relies on how the tests are run.
